messages:
maria: Heads up — since the overnight BIOS roll in us-central1 we've seen a spike in OOB watchdog resets causing GPUs to get fenced and provisioning to thrash. Not full outage but higher evictions and retry churn. :warning:
jamal: saw the alert, watching now. symptoms? are nodes failing POST or just watchdog kicks?
alex: nodes are hitting watchdog during BMC re-init after the microcode update, looks like timing regression. logs show repeated 'watchdog_triggered=true' and then pxe fallback.
maria: exact. affected racks are rack-7* and rack-9*. traffic is getting routed to other regions which is increasing egress and cost — noticed a 12% bump in cross-region allocations since 03:00 UTC.
sre_lead: tagging runbook owners @jamal @alex. Prioritize: 1) stop rollout 2) rollback firmware on canary pool 3) open capacity headroom 4) alert customers if we expect >5% SLA impact.
infra-bot: [ALERT] oob-watchdog-spike detected in us-central1, affected_nodes=18, fenced_gpus=42, incident_id=INC-20260317-42
jamal: I'm pausing the remaining BIOS batch now. command: `fleetctl firmware pause --batch=2026-03-17-bios-3`
alex: good. I'm preparing a rollback image with prior microcode (tag: bios-3-prev) and a conservative BMC watchdog timeout. will test on rack-7c first.
maria: for mitigation we should increase autoscale headroom in us-central1 and temporarily lower cross-region routing for low-priority jobs. cost hit short-term but reduces SLA blips.
lucy: can we also disable secure-boot toggles that were part of the patch? those toggles seem to correlate with longer BMC init sequences. if safe, revert toggle.
jamal: yes we can flip the toggle via the management plane: `rbctl set-secureboot --nodes rack-7* --state=enabled/disabled` — I'll set to previous state for canary.
alex: test logs from rack-7c after rollback prep: ```[2026-03-17T03:12:45Z] bmc_init: start
[2026-03-17T03:12:47Z] microcode_load: ok
[2026-03-17T03:12:51Z] watchdog_triggered=false
[2026-03-17T03:12:55Z] gpu_attach: success```
maria: nice. timeline: jamal pauses rollout 03:21, alex deploys rollback to canary 03:28, monitor for 30m, if stable then roll forward with longer watchdog timeout and toggle disabled.
sre_lead: add a cost note for finance: short-term cross-region surge ~12% due to rerouting and provisioning retries, estimate $4k/hr until stable. I put a hold on non-critical batch jobs in us-central1.
jamal: can we also gate future BIOS releases with a quick OOB loop test to ensure BMC init < 4s? add to preflight.
alex: will add a CI preflight that boots a small emu cluster and asserts bmc_init latency < 4s and secureboot toggle roundtrip < 2s.
maria: thanks team. next update in 20. I created INC-20260317-42 and pinned the runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incident/INC-20260317-42
infra-bot: [UPDATE] rollback applied to rack-7c at 03:34, monitoring.
lucy: early signs look good, no further fencing for the canary after 6m. :thumbsup:
sre_lead: keep monitoring 1h then decide slow rollout vs full rollback. also capture evicted pod IDs for customer impact reports.
maria: noted. will compile notes and cost impact for the postmortem. thanks all.
